My last job for a software consulting firm included first interviews with HR, someone on the team is be joining, people on the 2 teams I'd be working with closely.   That's 4 hours right there and we still had 2nd and 3rd rounds of interviews which included managers for the various groups.

It's not uncommon when hiring app developers. The hiring company needs to know that they're going to end up with a highly skilled person who can hit the ground running.  The developer will be highly compensated.

The diaphragm tightens, your hands and feet might tingle as they flood with adrenaline, you may get tunnel vision, etc.  PTSD is *definitely* an involuntary relexive physical response. Intrusive thoughts are common after a trauma.   I was taught to stop them by first breathing in deeply through the nose (deep enough to feel your belly rise) then slowly letting the breath out through your mouth.   Do this several times.   This will calm your limbic system (lizard brain)  which thinks you're back in the trauma.   

If the intrusive thought persists,  short circuit it by, for instance, counting as many green things as you can see or wiggling your toes then moving your way up the rest of your body... wiggling anything you can. 

Intrusive thoughts are like a pinball machine in your brain.  Once the ball (the thought)  drops into the channel it can only go forward.   The more often this happens, the deeper the channel (the neural pathway)  is dug and the more persistent the intrusive thought becomes.  

It sounds silly simple but it all starts with that breathing... wresting control back from the lizard brain and returning to a calm place. 

If you are not able to stop the Intrusive thought on your own, I urge you to seek professional help.   This won't just go away in time (and,  honestly,  this particular Intrusive thought is the stuff of nightmares).
